limitations_and_boundaries: LeanDojo Benchmark's challenging split requires generalization to novel premises, but performance degrades on this split compared to random split.
ReProver does not use domain-specific pretraining or reinforcement learning, which could further improve performance.
LeanDojo still has a 1.4% proof-checking error rate, with documented failure cases.
Training and evaluation were conducted on specific hardware (single A100, eight V100s) and within time limits (10 minutes per proof).

experiments_or_tasks: Construct LeanDojo Benchmark: a dataset of 98,734 theorems/proofs extracted from mathlib with a challenging data split requiring generalization to novel premises.
Develop LeanDojo: an open-source toolkit for extracting data from Lean and interacting with the proof environment programmatically.
Develop ReProver: a retrieval-augmented LLM-based prover that uses a retriever to select premises from the math library.

methods.name: ReProver
methods.protocol_description: Retrieval-Augmented Prover: Given the current proof state, it retrieves a small number of premises from the math library using a DPR-based retriever, then generates a tactic using a ByT5 encoder-decoder model. The retriever is restricted to accessible premises and trained with in-file negative examples. Training takes 120 GPU hours on a single A100.

methods.name: LeanDojo toolkit
methods.protocol_description: Open-source tool for extracting data from Lean and interacting with the proof environment. Extracts fine-grained premise annotations, computes accessible premises via program analysis, and reduces proof-checking errors from 21.1% to 1.4% compared to lean-gym.
